cohort: 1,278,151 women with singleton, nonanomalous births in California from 2007 to 2011
finding: Maternal hospitalization costs were significantly higher for elective induction of labor compared to spontaneous labor, regardless of parity, mode of delivery, and gestational age at delivery.
mod_finding: This study found that elective induction of labor was associated with higher maternal hospitalization costs regardless of parity, mode of delivery, and gestational age at delivery.
